workspace-bound-agent-grant-01.graded_text: Each agent connection is bound to one firm workspace chosen at consent and approved by that firm's Admin, and a consultant who works for several firms makes a separate connection for each.

votes.e: D/project/docs/agent-access.md:17 says "Every agent connection is bound to exactly one firm workspace, and that binding never changes." Line 20: "During consent, the consultant picks one of their workspaces." Line 21: "To work with a second firm, the consultant authorizes the same resource again and picks the other workspace. That second connection needs its own approval from that firm's Admin." Line 42: "An Admin approves, and can narrow the capabilities".

workspace-bound-agent-grant-02.graded_text: The server checks on every call that the target belongs to the connection's bound workspace and that the consultant's membership and role are still live, so removal from a firm cuts off an existing connection.

votes.e: D/project/docs/agent-access.md:55 says "The consultant must still be a member of the bound workspace right now, checked against the provider's membership data, and the role comes from that same check. If the membership is gone, the call fails closed and the connection is moved to `revoked` with reason `membership_ended`." Line 57: "Every query runs against the bound workspace. A workpaper ID from another workspace returns the same `not_found`". Line 56 intersects the current role, the approval and the token scopes.

workspace-bound-agent-grant-03.graded_text: The design offers no connection whose scope spans more than one firm.

votes.e: Checked D/project/docs/agent-access.md, D/answer.txt and D/diff.txt (the only change). Line 22 says "No account-wide grants. One credential covering all of a consultant's memberships would break constraint 1 by construction, so we don't offer one, not even as an option." The closest line is 19, "a single OAuth protected resource", which is a single endpoint and not a multi-firm grant.
